text:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: [P2] High 5xx rate observed from /v1/generate in prod. Automatic alert triggered 1961234567. Affected tenants: acme-inc (partial), beta-analytics (full). Symptoms: pod restarts, GPU node evictions, increased latency. Page sent to jamie (oncall).

jamie (oncall): Ack — I'm on it. Kicking off triage. First look at k8s.

liam (eng-sre): In cluster: several nodes in GPU pool showing kernel/reset messages. Listing problematic node names: gpu-host-47, gpu-host-52. dmesg on gpu-host-47 shows frequent AER/PCIe messages. Pasting clipped serial output below.

liam (eng-sre): ```
[ 12345.678901] pcieport 0000:01:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: severity=Corrected
[ 12345.679012] pcieport 0000:01:00.0: AER: Multiple 'uncorrected' errors - resetting port
[ 12345.679123] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679234] nvidia: GPU device 0000:01:00.0: GPU reset detected
[ 12345.680000] kernel: device pci0000:00:01.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Uncorrected (Non-Fatal), type=Transaction
```

sana (infra): I see node eviction events in kube: pods on gpu-host-47 went to CrashLoopBackOff at 11:07. I'm going to cordon and drain gpu-host-47 now to prevent further impact while we investigate.

kevin (runtime): Can we enable fallback routing for critical customers to non-GPU endpoints or lower-tier model? I can flip the route for acme-inc to dedicated-1 fallback pool to stop user-facing errors.

marta (cs): acme support: we're seeing ~20% 5xx rate and a few customers reporting token generation failures. CS notified customers about potential degraded performance.

jamie (oncall): Timeline so far: 11:03 alert, 11:04 ack, 11:07 first node eviction (gpu-host-47), 11:10 cordon+drain started, 11:12 routing fallback applied for acme-inc, 11:22 additional evictions on gpu-host-52, 11:30 cloud provider reports host-level PCIe errors on both hosts.

liam (eng-sre): Collected additional cloud serial logs and kernel oops. Also see messages referencing ECC count increments on host NIC/GPU. Hypothesis 1: PCIe AER propagation from a noisy neighbor or hardware degradation causing GPUs to drop off bus and host to evict pods. Hypothesis 2: Recent kernel/firmware change on host images exposed a driver regressing behavior. Hypothesis 3: Cloud hypervisor transient DMA corruption.

sana (infra): Mitigations applied: cordon gpu-host-47 and gpu-host-52, migrated critical pods to spare hosts, and reprovisioned two new nodes from pool. I also opened a ticket with cloud provider (GCP case 12345678) to request hardware telemetry for the hosts.

kevin (runtime): For immediate customer continuity I increased replicas on model-service to 4 and toggled traffic split to prefer dedicated-1 pool (non-affected). Rolling restart of affected pods completed at 11:45.

liam (eng-sre): Sharing commands used for log collection: 
```
# serial console capture
gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output gpu-host-47 --zone=us-central1-a --port=1
# dmesg tail
ssh core@gpu-host-47 'sudo journalctl -k -u kernel -n 200'
```

jamie (oncall): Customer impact summary to include in incident page: acme-inc partial failures ~20% 11:03-11:45, beta-analytics degraded throughput 11:03-11:30, other tenants no sustained errors. No data loss reported.

marta (cs): Confirming CS banner sent at 11:25. We'll follow up with customers after RCA.

liam (eng-sre): Additional evidence: nv-host-trace shows GPU reset storms correlated with PCIe AER logs. Attaching snippet: 
```
[trace] reset_count: gpu-host-47: gpu0=7 gpu1=2 in last 30m
[trace] pci_err_count: pci0000:00:01.0=13
```

sana (infra): Cloud provider returned host hardware telemetry: uncorrectable ECC on PCIe link and repeated AER events. They recommended swapping the host hardware and offered to migrate VMs. We accepted and initiated live-migration for affected instances where possible.

kevin (runtime): Can we capture a list of pods that observed OOM vs GPU resets? I want to differentiate infra eviction vs app-level memory issues.

liam (eng-sre): Quick grep across kube events: 
```
kubectl get events -A --field-selector reason=Evicted | grep gpu-host-47
# shows evictions with reason: NodeHasSufficientMemory false and Followed by KernelReset events
```

jamie (oncall): Summary of actions and owner assignment: 
- Owner (immediate): jamie - coordinate mitigation and customer comms
- Technical lead for RCA: liam (eng-sre) - collect serial logs, kernel traces, nv-host traces
- Infrastructure owner: sana - liaise with cloud provider, reprovision/replace hosts
- Runtime owner: kevin - ensure routing fallback and model resiliency changes are tracked
- Customer comms: marta (cs)

liam (eng-sre): Hypotheses to track in RCA thread: [H1] Hardware PCIe link degradation (noisy neighbor or cable) -> Evidence: AER/uncorrected ECC counts, cloud telemetry. [H2] Driver/firmware regression -> Evidence required: compare host images and kernel versions on affected vs healthy hosts. [H3] Hypervisor DMA corruption -> Evidence required: cross-tenant error correlation and cloud provider feedback.

sana (infra): I've uploaded full serial logs and kernel vmcore to our internal object store at s3://redwood-incident-logs/1961234567/ and added cloud ticket updates.

kevin (runtime): Noted we toggled fallback and scaled replicas; action item to revert fallback after nodes are verified and stable.

jamie (oncall): Current status at 13:00: traffic routed away from affected hosts, new nodes provisioned, customer-impact window narrowed to 11:03-11:45 for most tenants. Leaving incident open for RCA and postmortem.

liam (eng-sre): Creating RCA doc and checklist: will include timeline, log attachments, hypothesis testing steps, and recommended mitigations (firmware update, PCIe cable/slot replacement, host reprovisioning policy, improved alerting for AER counts). Assigning RCA ticket INC-2026 to liam/sana.

kevin (runtime): I'll add a follow-up to consider automatic fallback when node-level AER counts exceed threshold and a playbook for draining node before pod eviction.

marta (cs): Will prepare customer-facing summary once RCA draft is available.

jamie (oncall): Thanks everyone. If anything new appears ping the channel. Closing live mitigation loop; RCA work continues.
